$comment: Configuration of the M03 native runs (m03-plan §4) for m03-evidence.py (tests/native/m02/m02-evidence.py with the M03 constants). TEMPLATE: no native run has happened yet. The native-run unit sets build_commit, started_at, artifacts_root (one directory per build, e.g. tests/evidence/artifacts/m03/exit-<commit>), environment, artifact digests and commands, regenerates tests/native/m03/required-inventory.json at that commit (with fresh --scan reports for the Linux and Windows builds, which add the platform-only tests the build host cannot list), and only then runs --write. Every logs, commands_logs and facts path below is relative to artifacts_root; a missing file stops the generator before anything is written. macos/docker.txt is the macOS harness's run of the #[ignore = "docker: …"] cases (HM_DOCKER_TESTS=1 after up.sh), listed after check.txt so that a passing result there replaces the `ignored` the plain run logged. The lock procedure's checks (tests/native/m03/lock-macos.sh, lock-windows.ps1) and the Windows interactive harness ports are added by the integrator.
commands: tests/native/m03/refresh-inventory.sh (regenerates tests/native/m03/required-inventory.json at the exit commit, with the Linux and Windows scans)
tests/native/m03/run-macos.sh <artifacts_root> (writes macos/: check.sh, the observation pass, the Docker phase)

on the PC, by a T3 agent at Medium integrity: pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/native/m03/run-windows-local.ps1 -Commit <exit commit> -ScratchRoot <scratch root>; then on the build host: python3 -I tests/native/m02/import-windows-bundle.py --bundle <report> --label <artifacts_root name> --commit <exit commit> --artifacts-root tests/evidence/artifacts/m03 --config <artifacts_root>/runs.json

on the PC, inside the controller distribution, after the Windows run: HM_LOCAL=1 HM_PREBUILT_HEIMDALL=<linux heimdall> HM_PREBUILT_SHA256=<its sha256> HM_WSL_ROOTFS=<pinned image> HM_WSL_ALLOW_APT=1 bash tests/native/m03/run-wsl-distro.sh <out>/wsl-distro, and the M02 scenario at the same build: bash tests/native/m02/run-wsl-distro.sh <out>/wsl-distro-m02 (same inputs)

tests/native/m03/lock-macos.sh <artifacts_root>/macos-lock and, on the PC, tests/native/m03/lock-windows.ps1 -ProductBin <release heimdall.exe> -Driver <e2e_exit_m03.exe> -SignalTest <integration_session_lock.exe> -Commit <exit commit> -Out <dir> (ADR-0004 §2 lock rule; bound to the exit commit), imported with --platform-dir windows-lock
common_limitations: Status discipline (m03-plan §3, M01 rule E15): verified rows mean the required tests ran and passed on that platform in this run; not an independent review of the units. The lowest-row rule applies: a blocked owner-input row (m03-plan §7, B1-B13) keeps its record blocked, and no claim is widened to cover it.

Debug test builds on the test store are mechanism evidence only: only a release-profile run on a product store kind can carry a custody claim (ADR-0008 D12 item 3, F03); in M03 that is the Windows DPAPI row alone. The macOS lock_continuity claim stays not_verified (B3).

Linux and Windows binaries are cross-built on the macOS host with zig and run natively on the hosts (Windows: built and run natively on the PC); tests that read the repository at its compile-time path run on the build host only (case-index.json build_host_paths): a platform-neutral one counts as run elsewhere, any other keeps its row in_progress (harness gap).
The Docker cases (#[ignore = "docker: …"]) run on the macOS build host only (HM_DOCKER_TESTS=1 after up.sh): the devbox has no Docker (B8) and the Windows PC runs the fixture sshd in WSL scratch.
Proptest regression files resolve at compile-time source paths: persisted regression seeds replay on macOS only; the fixed default seeds run everywhere.

Every fixture is disposable: per-run keys, the loopback fixture sshd, disposable ssh-agents with a scratch HOME, scratch configuration, scratch and disposable file keychains, a disposable WSL distribution; the owners' keys, agents, keychains, ~/.ssh and Git configuration are never test material (m03-plan §0.2).

macos-lock.label: macos-arm64 lock procedure (debug build, test store: mechanism evidence only)

windows-lock.label: windows-11-x86_64 lock procedure (release profile, product DPAPI store)

A03.summary: Lock continuity: fresh authentications continue through desktop and vault lock without the original vault staying unlocked; the lock-revokes alternative behaves differently and is disclosed once (R-UX-03); the process-restart re-issue row. macOS is mechanism evidence (debug build, test store); Windows is the release-profile product DPAPI row.
limitations: macOS lock rows are a debug build on the test store: mechanism evidence, never the macOS lock_continuity claim (B3, F03).

Blocked: the macOS login-keychain product row (B3), the Linux desktop row (B11), the 1Password vault row (B1) and the Windows system-agent vault row (B4); the lock-procedure checks (a03_*) are native steps apart from the exit build window (m03-plan §4.4).

Lock-revokes grant R (ADR-0008 D7; the orchestrator's ruling on I-11): a session_locked revocation is local and immediate. R's tombstone commits with its move to revoking, and every fresh login of R through Heimdall's endpoint is refused from then on (the attribution check: 0 of R's key IDs accepted after the revocation). R stays revoking while its certificates' residual is pending, that is until their latest valid_before (R's deadline, about 2 h after R was created) has passed on safe time; the supervisor then moves it to revoked. It never returns to active. m03-plan §4.4 step 6 ("ended for good") is met by revoking -> revoked, the refused logins and no reactivation; a run that ends before the residual passes records revoking, and R's window is not shortened to observe revoked.

A07.summary: Revocation: new local use fails immediately; descendants and stale callbacks cannot reactivate; remote-pending effects and the maximum residual are truthful; the generation is rechecked before issuance and activation (R-SE-07); the linearization model with re-issue, lock revocation and the signing gate.
limitations: The disconnected-runner variant of A07 is deferred_with_decision to M06 (G07; plan §5 M06); A07's M01 model rows stay as recorded.

A09.summary: Enrollment: existing access survives; only owned records change (R-CR-06); uncertain outcomes reconcile; newer edits are not overwritten; rotation and rollback; Docker, loopback and WSL default-path rows by platform.
limitations: The registry script's remove window is a disclosed limitation (m03-plan U5): a remote edit made inside it is lost and reported; revision 2's fence window is closed (§17.4 item 2).
Blocked: enrollment with 1Password as the existing access (B1), with the Windows system agent (B4) and with a touch-required key (B6).

A10.summary: Scope and issuer: only the intended access succeeds where enforcement is claimed; no issuer key or broader certificate escapes; unsupported scope is labelled; production verification per client and per form.
limitations: Blocked: the Linux Secret Service reachability row (B11).
The bound-consumer reachability recording (a10_bound_consumer_issuer_reachability_recorded) is added with the exit suite.

A23.summary: Deadlines and connections: owned admission and closure match the policy; no certificate-only enforcement assumption; unmanaged and remote-process limits are reported accurately; OpenSSH stop behaviour tested. Windows reports and enforces multiplexing as unavailable (verified).
limitations: Windows has no owned multiplexing (M-F7): the refusal and CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE are verified, not the masters.

A33.summary: Secrets: no secret leakage or plaintext fallback; previewed and redacted outputs; nothing collected by default.
limitations: Support bundles and update artifacts are deferred_with_decision to M08.
release_build_refuses_m03_test_gates exists only in a release-profile test build; its binary half is check.sh's release-gate step.

R-AU-08.summary: Reports show actual enforcement and reject unmet minimums (the managed report, claims, capability_unavailable for an unmet offline bound).
limitations: The claims-table rule (a debug build or test store never satisfies a custody claim) is enforced by tools/validation/claims_table.py (check.sh claims-table), not by a Cargo test.

background-once.summary: plan §5 M03 exit: the user can allow background work once without routine unlocks, within one boot (fixture level plus the A03 native rows); after a reboot the runtime start and one attended time confirm are counted as chores.
limitations: Blocked: the human walkthrough (B7) and the native reboot and logout rows (B12).

no-self-renewal.summary: plan §5 M03 exit: an expired grant cannot renew itself (renewal never extends the deadline or pairs; revoke-on-lock grants are never re-issued; issuer ceilings; the M01 A05 model rows).

honest-limits.summary: plan §5 M03 exit: no claim that all remote processes terminate or that all offline credentials revoke immediately (remote_processes not_terminated; revocation.remote unknown until its claim; bounded and nominally expired residuals).

fixed-provider.summary: plan §5 M03 exit: a fixed provider remains usable under its real limitations; the M02 A11 and A35 suites re-run unchanged at the M03 build, and the existing identity is untouched by enrollment.
limitations: References the M02 A11/A35 rows at the M03 build; the carried blocked rows stay blocked (B1, B4, B6).

store-macos-keychain.summary: K_ca custody, macOS (ADR-0005 §5.2): the keychain code path against a disposable file keychain (mechanism); the login-keychain product row is blocked.
limitations: Mechanism evidence only (debug build, disposable file keychain): no custody claim.
Blocked: the macOS login-keychain product row (B3) and the data-protection keychain row (B13).

store-windows-dpapi.summary: K_ca custody, Windows (ADR-0005 §5.2): the DPAPI CurrentUser blob in scratch, round trip across processes, owner-only DACL.
limitations: Only the windows-11 row is DPAPI evidence; the other platforms' rows run the scratch-store mechanism tests.
Blocked: cross-user unprotect refusal (B2).

store-linux-secret-service.summary: K_ca custody, Linux (ADR-0005 §5.2): the headless devbox reports issuer_store_unavailable and writes no plaintext; the Secret Service row is blocked.
limitations: Blocked: Secret Service over DH and availability after login need a Linux desktop host (B11).

sleep-logout-reboot.summary: ADR-0005 §9.3 P2, P3, P4, P-W2 and R4: the process-restart rows and the virtual-clock sleep rows run; native sleep, logout and reboot are blocked.
limitations: Blocked: native sleep, logout and reboot rows (B12; the macOS logout row also B3).

M03 exit cases (m03-plan §3).summary: m03-plan §3: every M03 exit case and claim per platform, all rows from one build; blocked while any owner-input row (B1-B13) is blocked (the lowest-row rule).

P1.summary: ADR-0005 §9.3 P1, macOS screen lock (mechanism evidence: debug build, test store)
limitations: Mechanism evidence only: a debug build on the test store never yields the macOS lock_continuity claim, which waits for a release-profile run on the login keychain of a disposable account (B3; F03). Supersedes tests/evidence/g04-macos-screen-lock-probe.json.

limitations: Only a release-profile run on the product DPAPI store is claim-eligible (F03). Supersedes tests/evidence/g04-windows-desktop-lock-probe.json.
